content.title: Zn-Air and Lithium-ion Batteries
content.description: Zn-air and Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are advanced electrochemical energy storage devices. Zn-air batteries use oxygen from the atmosphere, while Li-ion batteries use reversible movement of lithium ions between electrodes.

content.content: Modern batteries are designed to provide high energy density, long service life, and reliable performance. Zn-air batteries are lightweight and economical, whereas Lithium-ion batteries are rechargeable and widely used in portable electronics and electric vehicles.

content.title: Key Difference
content.content: Zn-air batteries are primary (generally non-rechargeable), whereas Lithium-ion batteries are secondary (rechargeable).

A Zn-air battery consists of a zinc anode, an air cathode, and an alkaline electrolyte (KOH). Oxygen from the atmosphere acts as the cathode reactant, making the battery lightweight and energy efficient.

A Lithium-ion battery consists of a graphite anode, a lithium metal oxide cathode, an organic electrolyte, and a separator. During charging and discharging, lithium ions move between the electrodes, making the battery rechargeable.

items.question: Zn-Air Battery
items.answer: Used in hearing aids, medical devices, navigation equipment, and backup power systems.

items.question: Lithium-ion Battery
items.answer: Used in smartphones, laptops, cameras, drones, and power tools.

items.question: Li-ion Battery in Electric Vehicles
items.answer: Used in electric cars, buses, scooters, and bicycles due to high energy density and long life.

items.question: Advantages for EVs
items.answer: Provides fast charging, lightweight construction, high efficiency, low maintenance, and zero tailpipe emissions.

content.title: Why Li-ion Batteries are Preferred for EVs
content.content: Lithium-ion batteries offer high energy density, longer driving range, faster charging, low self-discharge, and excellent rechargeability, making them ideal for electric vehicles.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Zn-air batteries use zinc and atmospheric oxygen.
Li-ion batteries are rechargeable secondary batteries.
Graphite is commonly used as the anode in Li-ion batteries.
Li-ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles.
High energy density and long cycle life are major advantages of Li-ion batteries.
